messages:
Maya Patel: Heads up — we need to request a bunch of network quotas for ap-south-1 before next week's GPU capacity run. We're planning ~120 GPU nodes (mixed A10/A100) across 3 AZs. Current EIP quota is 5 in that account/region, and our ENI/secondary IP headroom looks tight. Can someone take point on filing support?

Omar Reyes: I can take it. Quick Qs: do we plan to give every node a public EIP, or are we using NAT + a few bastions/NLBs? That changes how many EIPs we actually need.

Maya Patel: We should avoid per-node public IPs where possible — Priya's team will try to use NAT for outbound. But we still need: ~8 static EIPs for NLBs/bastions and ~100 spare EIPs for emergency direct-access debug tunnels the infra team asked for (we use them occasionally for perf debugging). Also need ENI/secondary-private-IP increases because our CNI attaches extra ENIs for SR-IOV sidecars and we plan >2 secondary IPs per node.

Priya Nair: Strong preference: minimize EIP count (cost + limits). Can we instead reserve a pool of NAT Gateways + Elastic IPs behind NLBs and use ephemeral SSH tunnels? If AWS will approve a big EIP quota it's fine, but let's note cost: EIPs incur hourly charges when unused.

Jin Wu: Practical constraints: for the GPU jobs we run, we often need direct node access for CUDA debug, so we still want the option to assign an EIP quickly. But 100 EIPs seems high. How about we ask for 40 EIPs and a plan to request more if needed? Also need ENI per instance and total ENI quotas increased — some of our gpu instance types need 8-15 ENIs each depending on config.

Omar Reyes: OK I will open a support case. Proposed ask: EIP quota to 200 (to be safe for growth), ENI quota per region increase (total ENIs) to 8k, increase "IPv4 addresses per subnet" operational headroom by creating new /22 subnets in each AZ (we'll handle VPC changes), and enable IPv6 (dualstack) at account level so we can offload public egress to IPv6 NAT where possible. Also request higher secondary-private-IP quota (for ENI attachments) to 6000. Thoughts?

Priya Nair: Numbers look conservative. I endorse smaller EIP immediate ask (40) + auto-approval path later, but Omar knows the next two quarters roadmap. If support wants justification we can point to: planned 120 nodes, 3 AZs, k8s CNI needing X IPs per pod, and expected burst capacity.

Maya Patel: Filing with the higher numbers now avoids repeated tickets — go for the larger ask and we can scale down if they push back. Please include the timeline (we need approvals in 7 business days).

Omar Reyes: Filed support case: 1234567890 (opened). Payload summary in the case: request EIP quota increase to 200 in ap-south-1, increase EC2 ENI quota to 8000, increase per-instance ENI limit for GPU instance family to 50, request additional secondary private IP quota to 6000, request guidance/enablement for account-level IPv6 in ap-south-1. Attached Terraform plan and projected pod IP usage.

aws-support-bot: Hi team — case 1234567890 created. Initial response expected within 24-48 hours. Reference id: SR-AP-2026-0001. Note: IPv6 enablement requires VPC-level changes and possibly org-level approval; we've flagged the request with the networking team.

(24 hours later) aws-support-bot: Update on SR-AP-2026-0001 — AWS is asking for a short justification doc and the expected peak concurrent instances. Please reply with: (1) expected concurrent GPU hosts (not total) during peak, (2) whether EIPs will be associated 24/7 or ephemeral, (3) whether you can use NAT+LoadBalancer pattern instead of per-node EIPs.

Maya Patel: Replying now: expected peak concurrent GPU hosts = 120, EIPs will be ephemeral in ~80% of cases, 8 static for prod NLBs/bastions. We'll include cost/ops justification and fallbacks.

(2 business days) aws-support-bot: Partial approval granted for SR-AP-2026-0001. Updates: EIP quota increased to 200 (ap-south-1) — approved, total ENI quota increased to 6000 (temporary increase; can request permanent bump), per-instance ENI limit for GPU family set to 40, secondary private IP quota increased to 4500. IPv6: AWS confirmed account-level dualstack can be enabled but requires a scheduled maintenance window to enable on existing VPCs; we've attached the checklist. Case updated: 1234567890 — closure pending your confirmation.

Omar Reyes: Nice. I'll capture the new quotas in our capacity docs and update Terraform modules and quota-alerting.

Priya Nair: I'll adjust the cost model for EIP usage and add reminder to release EIPs when not associated. Also let's create a runbook for attaching EIPs for debug so it's not ad-hoc.

Jin Wu: I'll schedule a short maintenance window to enable IPv6 on the test VPC next week and validate NAT64/e2e routing.

Maya Patel: Thanks all. Omar — please mark the case resolved once you apply the changes in infra and confirm the VPC work. :thumbsup:

Omar Reyes: Will do. Filing follow-ups: I'll open an internal ticket to create new /22 subnets in each AZ and update the nodepool subnet assignment. ETA: Terraform changes in next PR.

aws-support-bot: Noted. If you need further increases after rollout, reopen SR-AP-2026-0001 or create a new request. Closing update logged at 1823457420.
